properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 9 at 12:00PM PDT until October 12 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday afternoon. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:

30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 7:57AM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by around Tuesday of next week. This
trough is likely to remain strong and active through the duration
of next week, and may even intensify with embedded low pressure
centers. Widespread showers may be heavy and persistent at times
with the possibility of thunderstorms Tuesday through the weekend.
Widespread flash flooding may occur from this rainfall.
Landslides will be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
While there is still uncertainty in the exact magnitude and
duration of rainfall, plan now for wet conditions next Tuesday
through Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Tuesday through Sunday of next week

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 9 at 11:53AM MST until October 12 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Yavapai, western Coconino, northern Gila, and far southern
Navajo counties.

* WHEN...From Saturday morning through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A upper-level trough will help pull moisture from the remnants of
Hurricane Rachel up into western Arizona to produce showers and
thunderstorms Saturday, followed by extended periods of rainfall
through at least Sunday. Thunderstorms will have the potential to
produce heavy rainfall that could lead to flash flooding, while
extended periods of rain can lead to elevated streams, rivers,
and flow through washes. Greatest risk of heavy rainfall looks be
along higher terrain due to upsloping.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Lee; Itawamba; Chickasaw; Monroe
properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 9 at 1:42PM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
HLSMEG

This product covers Mid-South

**TROPICAL STORM WARNING EXPANDED INTO PORTIONS OF NORTHEASTERN
MISSISSIPPI**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Chickasaw,
Itawamba, Lee MS, and Monroe

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Chickasaw, Itawamba,
Lee MS, and Monroe

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 420 miles south-southeast of Tupelo MS
- 28.4N 87.2W
- Storm Intensity 120 mph
- Movement North-northeast or 20 degrees at 16 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

After making forecast landfall along Alabama and Florida Coast as a
Category 3 hurricane, Isaias is forecast to begin making a northeastern
trek inland. The primary impacts with Isaias' remnants here in the
Mid-South will be gusty winds and periods of heavy rainfall. The latest
forecast from the NHC does have Isaias impacting portions of the Mid-
South at Tropical Storm strength. Though there still exists uncertainty
with the overall impacts, storm track, and intensity this far inland,
four of our counties are now in a Tropical Storm Warning through
tomorrow afternoon with wind gusts in excess of 40 mph in these areas.
These areas will also see rainfall amounts up to 3".


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across northeast Mississippi. Potential impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals,
arroyos, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across northeast Mississippi.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
northeast Mississippi. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Mid-South, little to no impact is anticipated.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Memphis TN as conditions warrant.

NWSheadline:
TROPICAL STORM WARNING EXPANDED INTO PORTIONS OF NORTHEASTERN
MISSISSIPPI

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 9 at 1:38PM CDT by NWS Twin Cities/Chanhassen MN
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Minnesota Pollution Control Agency has issued an Air
Quality Alert for coarse particles pollution. The Air Quality
Index (AQI) is expected to reach the Orange or Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups category.

* WHERE...West central and southwest Minnesota.

* WHEN...From 7 AM CDT to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Sensitive groups, such as people with lung disease
(including asthma), heart disease, and children and older
adults, may experience health effects.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Unseasonably warm temperatures and strong
southerly wind gusts in excess of 40 mph across dry soils in an
area of drought will result in blowing dust and reduced air
quality Saturday morning and afternoon. Decreasing winds will
lessen the potential for impacts through the evening.
properties.instruction:

asthma), heart disease, and children and older adults, should
limit prolonged or heavy exertion.

Reduce or eliminate activities that contribute to air pollution,
such as outdoor burning, and use of residential wood burning
devices. Reduce vehicle trips and vehicle idling as much as
possible.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 9 at 2:38PM EDT until October 11 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Marquette has issued a Red Flag
Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect
from noon EDT /11 AM CDT/ Saturday to 6 PM EDT /5 PM CDT/ Sunday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 002 Ontonagon and Fire
Weather Zone 009 Gogebic.

* TIMING...From noon EDT /11 AM CDT/ Saturday to 6 PM EDT /5 PM
CDT/ Sunday.

* WINDS...Saturday, south 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.
Sunday, south 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Saturday, as low as 32 percent. Recover to
55-60 percent Saturday night. Sunday, as low as 32 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures and
exceptionally dry fuels will create dangerous wildland fire
conditions. Campfires, outdoor grills, smoking materials,
fireworks, chain saws, and all-terrain vehicles all have the
potential to throw a spark and ignite a dangerous and destructive
fire.
